arxiv-2104-12752.description: Abstract The Euclid satellite, to be launched by ESA in 2022, will be a major instrument for cosmology for the next decades. Euclid is composed of two instruments: the Visible (VIS) instrument and the Near Infrared Spectromete and Photometer (NISP).

arxiv-2202-03504.title: Comprehensive analysis of TESS Full Orbital Phase Curve of WASP-121b
arxiv-2202-03504.creator: M.Eftekhar
arxiv-2202-03504.description: Abstract We present the full phase curve analysis of the ultrahot Jupiter WASP-121b ( R p ≃ 1.865 ​ R J , M p ≃ 1.184 ​ M J R_{p}\simeq 1.865R_{J},M_{p}\simeq 1.184M_{J} ) using observations from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and a comparison between our results with previous studies on this target.

arxiv-2303-14799.title: Subtractive spaces of semirings
arxiv-2303-14799.creator: Amartya Goswami
arxiv-2303-14799.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Amartya Goswami. Using the closure operator that defines a subtractive ideal of a semiring S S , in this note we introduce a topology on the set of all ideals of S S induced by that operator. We show that the corresponding subtractive space is T 0 T_{0} and every nonempty irreducible closed set has a unique generic point, whereas the restricted subspace of subtractive ideals is T 1 T_{1} .

arxiv-2308-05844.title: Finiteness of stable Lagrangian fibrations
arxiv-2308-05844.creator: Ljudmila Kamenova
arxiv-2308-05844.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ljudmila Kamenova. In memory of my dear friend Sasha Ananin

Abstract

In this paper we survey some finiteness results of the deformation classes
of hyperkähler Lagrangian fibrations, and we prove finiteness
for stable Lagrangian fibrations with a given discriminant divisor. 1
Introduction

In hyperkähler geometry a natural question to ask is whether there are
finitely many examples (up to deformation) in a given dimension. For the
known compact hyperkähler examples, this is indeed the case.

arxiv-2310-01281.title: An in-silico study of conventional and FLASH radiotherapy iso-effectiveness: Radiolytic oxygen depletion and its potential impact on tumor control probability e-mail:juan.pardo.montero@sergas.es
arxiv-2310-01281.creator: Isabel González-Crespo, Faustino Gómez, Óscar López Pouso, Juan Pardo-Montero
arxiv-2310-01281.description: Abstract FLASH radiotherapy (FLASH-RT) has shown the potential to spare normal tissue while seemingly maintaining the effectiveness of conventional radiotherapy (CONV-RT). It has been suggested that the protective effect arises from the radiolytic oxygen depletion (ROD) caused by FLASH-RT, but it is not entirely clear why this protective effect is not observed in tumors.

arxiv-2501-02129.title: Equivariant operads, symmetric sequences, and Boardman-Vogt tensor products
arxiv-2501-02129.creator: Natalie Stewart
arxiv-2501-02129.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Natalie Stewart. We advance the foundational study of be Nardin-Shah’s ∞ \infty -category of G G -operads and their associated ∞ \infty -categories of algebras. In particular, we construct the underlying G G -symmetric sequence of a (one color) G G -operad, yielding a monadic functor; we use this to lift Bonventre’s genuine operadic nerve to a conservative functor of ∞ \infty -categories, restricting to an equivalence between categories of discrete G G -operads.

arxiv-2504-08401.title: Graph Reduction with Unsupervised Learning in Column Generation: A Routing Application
arxiv-2504-08401.creator: Abdo Abouelrous, Laurens Bliek, Adriana F. Gabor, Yaoxin Wu, Yingqian Zhang
arxiv-2504-08401.description: Abstract Column Generation (CG) is a popular method dedicated to enhancing computational efficiency in large scale Combinatorial Optimization (CO) problems. It reduces the number of decision variables in a problem by solving a pricing problem. For many CO problems, the pricing problem is an Elementary Shortest Path Problem with Resource Constraints (ESPPRC).

arxiv-2511-14693.title: Talk, Snap, Complain: Validation-Aware Multimodal Expert Framework for Fine-Grained Customer Grievances
arxiv-2511-14693.creator: Rishu Kumar Singh, Navneet Shreya, Sarmistha Das, Apoorva Singh, Sriparna Saha
arxiv-2511-14693.description: Abstract Existing approaches to complaint analysis largely rely on unimodal, short-form content such as tweets or product reviews. This work advances the field by leveraging multimodal, multi-turn customer support dialogues—where users often share both textual complaints and visual evidence (e.g., screenshots, product photos)—to enable fine-grained classification of complaint aspects and severity.

arxiv-2511-22375.title: Maximum Entropy and Bayesian Conditioning Under Extended Space
arxiv-2511-22375.creator: Boning Yu
arxiv-2511-22375.description: Abstract This paper examines the conditions under which Bayesian conditioning aligns with Maximum Entropy. Specifically, I address cases in which newly learned information does not correspond to an event in the probability space defined on the sample space of outcomes.

pmc-10657323.title: Herpes zoster is not associated with subsequent gastrointestinal cancer: data from over 200,000 outpatients in Germany
pmc-10657323.creator: Catherine Leyh, Christoph Roderburg, Tom Luedde, Sven H Loosen, Karel Kostev
pmc-10657323.description: PurposeGastrointestinal (GI) cancers are an increasing global health challenge. Viral diseases play an important role in the development of GI cancers. For example, Epstein-Barr virus, which belongs to the human herpesvirus family, is a well-recognized risk factor for the development of gastric cancer.

pmc-11862096.title: COVID-19 Infection and Medicines in Pregnancy in Canada
pmc-11862096.creator: A. Berard, O. Sheehy, P. Kaul, S. Eltonsy, M. Walker, S. Hawken, S. Bernatsky, M. Pugliese, O. Barrett, A. Savu, R. Dragan
pmc-11862096.description: IntroductionAlthough over 100 million pregnant women worldwide are at risk of infection with SARS-CoV-2, little data exists on the impact of COVID-19 and related treatments on maternal/neonatal health.Objectives1) To quantify the prevalence of medication use in pregnancy to treat COVID-19; 2) To quantify and compare the risk of adverse pregnancy/neonatal outcomes in those with and without COVID-19.

pmc-12363105.title: The effect of non-insulin dependent insulin resistance indices on the prediction in the recurrence of late atrial fibrillation after modified maze procedure concomitant with valvular heart surgery
pmc-12363105.creator: Jianliang Liu, Min Lin, Yan Huang, Wenpeng Dong
pmc-12363105.description: ObjectiveSurgical ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF) is suitable for patients with AF undergoing concomitant cardiac surgery. However, the high rate of AF recurrence after surgery remains a significant clinical concern. This study examined the association between insulin resistance (IR) indices and late AF recurrence in patients undergoing modified maze surgery combined with valvular heart surgery.

pmc-12632052.title: Total bilirubin as a mortality predictor in non-elderly hemodialysis patients: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
pmc-12632052.creator: Yuyang Chen, Haowen Zhang, Hongyan Liu, Jialong Zhang, Xuan Dai, Wenjing Dong, Qingqing Liu, Liping Zhu, Yefan Zhang, Xue Zhou, Li Cheng, Xiaoyan Lu, Haixia Yang, Qian Liu, Jie Song, Qian Li, Jiarui Li, Haihua Su, Xinchao Tao, Aijie Shi, Pei Yu
pmc-12632052.description: BackgroundThe association between serum total bilirubin (TBIL) levels and mortality in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients, especially when stratified by age, has not been clearly established.MethodsWe performed a multicenter retrospective analysis of 409 MHD patients (40 deaths, 9.8%) over a median follow-up of 31.3 months (interquartile range (IQR), 28.9–31.8). Cox regression models evaluated TBIL’s predictive role for mortality.

pmc-12736770.title: Pharmacokinetic Landscape and Interaction Potential of SGLT2 Inhibitors: Bridging In Vitro Findings and Clinical Implications
pmc-12736770.creator: Nahyun Koo, Eun Ji Lee, Ji-Eun Chang, Kyeong-Ryoon Lee, Yoon-Jee Chae, Natalia V De Moraes, Vanessa Bergamin Boralli, Stephan Schmidt
pmc-12736770.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are widely used in type 2 diabetes and cardiometabolic diseases, and their pharmacokinetic characteristics generally confer a low risk of clinically relevant drug–drug interactions (DDIs). Most clinical studies demonstrate that these agents can be co-administered safely with commonly prescribed medications without dose adjustment, although strong enzyme inducers such as rifampin can reduce systemic exposure, and pharmacodynamic interactions may still arise.

pmc-12996011.title: From Subliminality, to the Unconscious Mind: Philosophical Lineages, Evolutionary Paradoxes, and the Future of the Origins of the Unconscious
pmc-12996011.creator: Myron Tsikandilakis, Persefoni Bali, Roland Erich Uriko, Victοria-Maria Pasachidou, Romina Leonor Toranzos, Konrad Szczesniak, Christopher Raj Madan, Pierre-Alexis Mével, Alison Grant Milbank
pmc-12996011.description: In previous works, we provided empirical evidence and the theoretical foundations for a conceptual dissociation between subliminality, such as purported emotional responses to invisible-imperceptible elicitors, and the intelligent workings of the notion of an unconscious mind, such as involuntary and automatic physiological experiences and behavioural patterns that precede but eventually interact with conscious awareness and evaluation.

pmc-13039678.title: Mesenchymal stromal cells modulate survival and regeneration of human hematopoietic stem cells via PGE2/cAMP signaling
pmc-13039678.creator: Siva Sai Naga Anurag Muddineni, Chen Katz-Even, Adi Zipin-Roitman, Diana Rasoulouniriana, Debanjan Singha Roy, Rabeaa Aborgies, Katia Beider, Yael Raz, Neta Solomon, Gal Hershkovitz, Yael Shulman, Rony Chen, Eviatar Weizman, Claudia Waskow, Arnon Nagler, Michael Milyavsky
pmc-13039678.description: Ionizing radiation and chemotherapy significantly impair hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) function, increasing the risk of bone marrow failure and secondary malignancies. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), critical regulators within the hematopoietic niche, maintain HSPC quiescence, self-renewal, survival, and differentiation. However, the specific pro-regenerative signaling pathways activated by MSCs in human HSPCs remain incompletely defined.

pmc-13189959.title: Development and preliminary evaluation of a ciliary muscle–oriented motor imagery script for primary school children: a school-based cluster randomized controlled trial
pmc-13189959.creator: Meng Zhang, Sheng Zhou, Xu Zhang
pmc-13189959.description: BackgroundMyopia in children is occurring earlier and progressing faster, while existing interventions such as outdoor activity and device-based visual training are often difficult to implement consistently in school settings. Motor imagery (MI), as a low-burden cognitive approach, may offer a complementary pathway for visual-function support. However, ciliary muscle–oriented MI scripts specifically designed for children remain underdeveloped.

pmc-13200665.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting Among Adult Cancer Patients at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital: A Prospective Study
pmc-13200665.creator: Patrick Kitheka Muasya, Tadele Mekuriya Yadesa, John Isiiko, Julius Kyomya, Joel Oenga, Abubakar Amina, Godwin Nimusiima, Sebisaalu Joel, John Martin Tumwebaza, Kabera Radiana Makuza
pmc-13200665.description: BackgroundChemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) remains a significant and distressing adverse effect of cancer treatment, adversely affecting patients’ quality of life. Despite well-established international guidelines for antiemetic prophylaxis, variability in CINV incidence and guideline adherence persists across different regions and healthcare settings, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

pmc-13239676.title: Age‐related macular degeneration severity and risk of Alzheimer's disease in older adults in a prospective, community‐based cohort study
pmc-13239676.creator: Chloe A. Krakauer, Luke Reilly, Yu‐Ru Su, Rod L. Walker, Dana Lee, Vilaipone A. Xaiyamuangchanh, David J. Cronkite, Nicole M. Gatto, Paul K. Crane, Emily Y. Chew, David E. Arterburn, Cecilia S. Lee
pmc-13239676.description: INTRODUCTIONAge‐related macular degeneration (AMD) is associated with higher risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD), but how AD risk changes as AMD progresses remains unclear.METHODSAmong participants in the Adult Changes in Thought study, we characterized the worst dry and wet AMD severities experienced to date on a scale of 0 to 10 and assessed whether they were associated with AD risk.

pmc-13683268.title: Impact of neck nodal yield on immune checkpoint inhibitor outcome after recurrence in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-13683268.creator: Dong Hyun Kim, Jiwon Koh, Yoon Kyung Jeon, Kyeong Cheon Jung, Jungirl Seok, Eun-Jae Chung, Seong-Keun Kwon, Soon-Hyun Ahn, Bhumsuk Keam
pmc-13683268.description: IntroductionNeck dissection and adequate lymph node yield (LNY) are important in the treatment of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Cervical lymph nodes represent the primary sites for T-cell priming; however, the impact of LNY on the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains unclear.
